challengeTypes: identify: Which of these is SYSTEM software? (Operating system vs Word processor vs Game vs Web browser)

sort: Drag each software to system or application software (Windows OS = System | MS Word = Application | Antivirus = System utility | Photoshop = Application | Linux = System | Calculator app = Application | Device driver = System | Tally = Application)

sort: Drag each OS function to its correct description (Memory management = allocates RAM to programs | File management = organizes files in folders | Process management = runs and schedules programs | Device management = controls hardware devices | User interface = provides way to interact | Security = protects from unauthorized access)

extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) System software — software that manages and controls computer hardware. Types: Operating System (Windows, Linux, macOS) — manages memory, files, processes, devices, provides user interface. Utility programs (antivirus, disk cleanup, defragmentation) — maintain and optimize the computer. Device drivers — allow the OS to communicate with hardware (printer driver, graphics driver). (2) Application software — software that performs specific tasks for users. General purpose: used for many purposes by many users (MS Word, Excel, Photoshop, web browser). Customised/specific purpose: designed for a specific organization or task (school management system, hospital management, banking software, Tally for accounting). (3) OSS, defragmentation, backup — Open Source Software (OSS): source code is freely available, anyone can view, modify, and distribute it. Examples: Linux, Firefox, LibreOffice, VLC. Proprietary software: owned by a company, source code is not available, must be purchased. Examples: Windows, MS Office, Photoshop. Defragmentation: rearranges fragmented file pieces on the hard disk so files are stored in continuous blocks, improving access speed. Backup: creating a copy of data so it can be restored if the original is lost or damaged. Types: full backup, incremental backup. Misconceptions: 'system software and application software are the same' (WRONG — system software manages hardware; application software performs tasks for users), 'the operating system is an application' (WRONG — the operating system is SYSTEM software that manages the computer), 'open source software is always free of cost' (PARTIALLY WRONG — OSS is free to use and modify, but some companies charge for support or enterprise versions), 'defragmentation deletes files' (WRONG — defragmentation only rearranges file fragments; it does not delete any files), 'backup is only needed for important businesses' (WRONG — everyone should backup their data; data loss can happen to anyone due to hardware failure, viruses, or accidents).
